question: Where do Layers and Library sit when something is picked?
context: Found while inventorying the panel on 2026-10-13: with a rectangle picked the panel shows Layers, Appearance, Effects, Motion, then Library; with a caliper picked it adds Measurements; on a video a title brings Captions and Transitions. Those lists are about the document, not the pick, and are what makes the panel feel clogged. Shipped already: a tool's settings only with that tool in hand, Masked by off measurements.

options.label: Pick on top, lists folded below
options.summary: The picked thing's sections lead the panel. Layers, Measurements, Library, Captions and Transitions sit under them, folded to their headers until you open one; an opened list stays open.
pros: The panel reads as the picked thing first, with almost nothing else in view
No new layout to learn: the same one column panel
cons: Picking from the Layers list needs a click to open it first
With a list open, picking a row moves that list down the panel under your pointer, by the height of the new pick's sections
options.mitigation: Folding remembers your choice, so someone who lives in Layers opens it once.

options.label: Pick on top, lists in a pane at the bottom
options.summary: The panel splits like Photoshop's Properties over Layers: the picked thing's sections scroll in the top part, and Layers, Measurements and Library share a pane at the bottom that keeps its height when the pick changes. A grip between them sets the split.
pros: Photoshop users find it where they expect it
Nothing jumps: picking a row never moves the list you clicked in
The pick's sections are always first
cons: Less height for each half on a laptop window
A bigger change to build than folding
options.mitigation: The bottom pane can be folded to its header with the same chevron every section has.

options.label: Lists on the left, the pick on the right
options.summary: Layers, Measurements and Library move to a sidebar on the left edge of the window, the way Figma and Final Cut place them; the right panel holds only the picked thing and the tool in hand.
pros: The right panel is short and never scrolls past a list
cons: Takes canvas width on both sides
Moves something every current user has learned to find on the right
options.mitigation: The left sidebar has its own toggle in the title bar and starts open only on a picture.

options.label: Keep the lists on top
options.summary: Layers stays at the top with the pick's sections under it, as today. Only the rule already shipped applies: no tool's settings with another tool in hand, no Masked by on a measurement.
pros: Picking a row never shifts the list
cons: The pick's own sections start below a list that can be tall
Library and the other lists still sit beside every pick
options.mitigation: Layers can be folded by hand, and the Sections menu can hide Library.
